content.text:
This confirms it directly: commit `004ec65b` (Dec 12, 2018) introduced the `maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap`/`maxSizeAfterFirstWrap` alignment logic in `setHalfwayBuffer`, unconditionally computing an "aligned" wrap size based on `atracBytesPerFrame`. The bug-fix commit `9caec286` (Dec 20, 2018, 8 days later) wraps that exact same computation in a new guard `if (readSize < bufferSize)`, falling back to the plain `bufferSize` values otherwise. This is the classic pattern of a fix that adds a missing precondition check to logic introduced in a prior commit — the original commit failed to account for the case where the buffer is already fully read (`readSize >= bufferSize`), causing the alignment arithmetic to produce an incorrect (too small or negative-relative) wrap boundary in that case.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 004ec65b0c329e37ea592c764fd48f9ab9a44fe1

## Reasoning
(1) I used `git log -S"maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap"` on `sceAtrac3plus.java` to find all commits that introduced or touched this specific variable, since the fix commit modifies logic built entirely around it. This returned exactly two commits: the fix itself (`9caec286`) and `004ec65b`, which is the commit that first introduced `maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap`/`maxSizeAfterFirstWrap`.

(2) In `004ec65b`, the previous simple call `new pspFileBuffer(addr, bufferSize, readSize, readSize)` was replaced with an unconditional computation of aligned wrap sizes: `maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap = bufferSize - ((bufferSize - info.inputFileDataOffset) % info.atracBytesPerFrame)` and `maxSizeAfterFirstWrap = bufferSize - (bufferSize % info.atracBytesPerFrame)`. This alignment was applied regardless of whether the halfway buffer was already fully populated (`readSize >= bufferSize`). The fix commit `9caec286` adds a guard (`if (readSize < bufferSize)`) so the alignment is only applied when the buffer isn't yet full, and additionally requires `maxSizeAligned >= readSize` before using the aligned value — otherwise it falls back to plain `bufferSize` for both parameters. This indicates the original unconditional alignment could produce a `maxSizeBeforeFirstWrap` smaller than `readSize` in the "buffer already full" case, causing incorrect/corrupted buffer wrap behavior (data being wrapped/read at the wrong offset).

(3) Evidence: the diff of `004ec65b` shows the exact code that `9caec286` later modifies to add the missing condition, with no other commit touching this logic in between (confirmed via `git log --oneline` on the file between the two commits, and `git log -S` showing only these two hits for the variable name). The fix commit's own inline comment — "If the buffer is not already full, try to align it..." — directly names the missing case that `004ec65b` failed to handle.

I'm confident in this identification since the fix is a narrowly-scoped, direct modification of the exact lines added in `004ec65b`, with no intervening commits altering that logic.
